req_desc:
First open main journey: exact seed on the list.
With no account, opening the landing route in a new browser shows the document list of a starter workspace holding exactly the Seed data records, with no sign-in screen and no spinner.

First open offline: reload keeps everything.
After the device is ready for offline use, a reload with no network opens the app shell, the same seeded list and every workspace route.

First open keyboard path: skip control and list order.
The first Tab stop is the skip control, which moves focus to the main region, and every list control and row is then reachable by Tab in visual order.

First open phone path: navigation closed and unreachable.
At the phone width the navigation starts closed, and while closed none of its links can be reached by Tab or found in the accessibility tree.

Block editing main journey: mixed blocks survive reload.
A document written with every text block type, a divider and a record table block shows the same blocks in the same order after a reload.

Block editing keyboard path: slash menu.
The slash menu opens from an empty block, filters as the person types, inserts the highlighted block with Enter, and closes with Escape with focus restored to the block.

Block editing keyboard path: indent and outdent.
Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent a list item within the published depth, and the published way out of the list leaves the editor by keyboard.

Block editing screen-reader path: saved announcement.
After an edit is durable on the device, the Announcements live region carries the published saved sentence, and never before that.

New document opens at once.
New document, online or offline, puts the document at the top of the list and opens it with focus in the title, with no spinner and no way to fail for connectivity.

Attachment block on the device.
A file added to a document while signed out shows the published waiting state and is still there after an offline reload.

Document list main journey: narrow, star, density.
Search, folder and tag narrow the list together, starring persists, and the chosen list density is remembered on this device across reloads.

Document list live update: count and rows in place.
The list and its count update in place on each keystroke, with no reload and with the scroll position kept.

Document list keyboard path: row action menu.
Every row is operable by keyboard, and its action menu works with arrow keys, Enter and Escape, with focus back on the opener.

Document list phone path: reduced row and tap targets.
At the phone width each row drops the published fields, and every control in the row meets the published tap size.

Saved filters.
The current search, folder and tag can be saved under a name, choosing the saved filter sets those controls to the saved values, and saved filters survive a reload.

Trash main journey: move and restore.
A document moved to trash leaves the list and appears on the Trash route, and Restore returns it to the list with its blocks intact.

Trash keyboard path: delete-forever dialog.
The delete-forever dialog names the document, keeps Tab inside it in both directions, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener.

Trash live update: two tabs.
Moving, restoring or deleting a document in one tab updates a second tab of the same browser within the published tab limit, with no reload.

Trash phone path: screen and confirmation.
The Trash screen and its confirmation fit the phone width with no sideways scrolling and with every control at the published tap size.

Deleted forever leaves the device.
A document deleted forever answers the published not-found screen at its address and is gone from the list, search, Trash and the canvas after a reload.

Page and canvas main journey: the Deal.
Pressing the view control deals the blocks from the sheet to their stored canvas positions in reading order, draws connectors only after the last card lands, and updates the URL view and selected block.

Page and canvas keyboard path: shortcut and focus.
The published shortcut switches views from any control in the document view, and focus stays on the same block in both views.

Page and canvas reversing motion: no jump mid-flight.
A second press during the motion reverses every card from where it is, with no jump, and ends in the other view with the URL and focus to match.

Page and canvas reduced motion: crossfade only.
With reduced motion on, no card travels, a short crossfade swaps the views, connectors appear at once, and end positions, URL, focus and announcement match the full motion.

Canvas arrange main journey: move, connect, independence.
Cards moved and connected keep their positions after a reload, reordering the page never moves a card, and moving a card never reorders the page.

Canvas arrange keyboard path: step, move, announce.
Every card is reached in reading order by Tab, is named with its type and label, moves by arrow keys, and each move is announced.

Canvas arrange phone path: pan and pinch.
One finger pans and two fingers pinch, zoom stays inside the published range, and the point under the fingers stays fixed.

Canvas arrange fit and zoom readout.
Fit to view brings every card inside the canvas region, and the zoom readout updates in place on every zoom change.

Deterministic card slots.
A block first opened on the canvas with no stored position gets the slot given by the published grid rule.

Records main journey: rows, typed columns, totals, board and back.
Rows and columns of every type can be added, the published totals are correct, and switching to the board and back keeps the data.

Records keyboard path: grid navigation and edit.
Arrow keys move between cells, Enter edits, and Escape cancels with the old value back and focus on the cell.

Records live update: totals and open editor.
The row count and column totals update in place on a filter or cell change, and an open cell editor keeps its caret and draft while a change arrives from another tab.

Records phone path: table scrolls in its own region.
At the phone width the table scrolls sideways inside its own region and the page never scrolls sideways.

Board main journey: moving a card changes the row.
The board groups rows by a single-select column, and moving a card changes that row's value in the table.

Board keyboard path: published move keys.
The published keys move a focused card between columns, focus stays on the card, and each move is announced.

Board phone path: touch drag and move menu.
On a touch device a card moves by dragging its grip or by the published non-drag menu, and both give the same result.

CSV round trip through the visible controls.
A table exported and imported through the visible controls keeps its values, and bad rows are skipped and reported with the published row-error copy.

CSV cells cannot run as formulas.
In an exported CSV every text, single-select and heading cell beginning with one of the published characters is neutralised as Business rules states.

Journal main journey: template once and days kept.
Today's note opens with the template body once, and moving between days keeps each day's writing.

Journal keyboard path: calendar grid.
Arrow keys move through the calendar grid, Enter opens the focused day, and focus stays on that day.

Journal two devices: one note, template once.
Two signed-in offline devices that open and write the same date end with one note holding both sets of writing and the template body once.

Journal phone path: calendar and note arrangement.
At the phone width the calendar sits above the note in one column with no sideways scrolling.

Journal date reads the same everywhere.
A note's date is the plain calendar date from the creating device and shows unchanged on a device in another time zone.

Templates main journey: browse, preview, copy.
The `Use this template` control adds a copy to the workspace and moves focus to that copy's title, and editing the copy leaves the original unchanged.

Templates keyboard path: preview dialog.
The preview dialog keeps Tab inside it, and Escape closes it with focus back on the card's preview control.

Templates exact text on card, preview and copy.
The card, the preview and the copied document show the published template text character for character.

Templates phone path: one column and chip row.
At the phone width the gallery is one column, and the category chips scroll sideways inside their own row while the page does not.

Sign-in and sync main journey: upload and second device.
A person signs up in the dialog and chooses upload, and a second context that signs in and chooses upload sees the merged workspace with nothing doubled.

Sign-in and sync keep-on-device choice.
Choosing to keep the workspace on this device sends none of it to the server, and a second context on the account sees none of it.

Sign-in and sync live update: edit reaches the other device.
An edit on one signed-in context appears in the other with no reload within the published online limit, and the sync sentence moves through its states.

Sign-in and sync keyboard path: dialogs by keys only.
The sign-in dialog and the upload choice can be completed by keys alone, with Tab kept inside each dialog and focus managed as published.

Account and session API.
The session, sign-up, sign-in and sign-out endpoints answer as the API section states, and being signed out is a normal 200 state.

Attachment storage API.
An attachment is reported stored only after object storage confirms it, is readable only by its owner, and is refused at the published limits.

Both kept main journey: both values on both devices.
The same block edited on two offline contexts shows both values under the Both kept marker on both after reconnecting, with neither lost.

Both kept keyboard path: choose by keys.
One value can be chosen with keys alone, focus lands on the published place, and both contexts settle on that value.

Both kept notice and unsynced mark.
The published Both kept notice shows word for word, and a block with unsynced changes carries the notch and its accessible-name text in both views.

Both kept screen-reader path: name and announcement.
The marker is part of the block's accessible name and the resolution is announced politely with the published sentence.

Share link API.
A share link reads one document only, cannot change anything, and stops working when revoked, regenerated, expired or its document is trashed or deleted.

Delete forever beats offline edits.
A document deleted forever stays gone after an offline device reconnects with edits to it, that device shows the published notice naming it, and its text and objects leave the server.

Storage outage screen.
While object storage is unavailable an attachment stays waiting on the device with the published sentences, and it becomes stored with no reload once storage returns.

Sync outage screen.
While the sync service is unreachable every local action still works and the published sentence shows with no error styling.

Share link reader page.
A link reader with no account sees the shared document alone, read-only, and the owner's Share dialog creates and copies the link.

Revoked link page.
After the owner revokes a link or makes a new one, the old address shows the published page in place of the document.

Device list screen.
Settings lists the account's devices, marks the current one, and removes another device through a confirmation, and that device then shows the published notice.

Device removal API.
Removing a device ends its session at its next request, and another account's device id answers not-found.

Sync status sentences.
The Sync status region always shows one of the four published states with its exact sentence, and each change of sentence reaches the Announcements region.

Accessibility on the main screens.
The main screens pass automated WCAG 2.2 AA checks with no violations and show a visible focus mark on every focusable control.

Published pane layouts.
Each published viewport shows exactly the pane layout published for it.

No sideways scrolling.
No main screen scrolls the page sideways at any of the three published viewports.

Closed panels are unavailable.
A closed navigation drawer or inspector is not visible, not reachable by Tab and not in the accessibility tree, at each viewport where it can close.

Colour scheme remembered.
Light, dark and system schemes apply at once and are remembered on this device across reloads.

Health, status and boot.
The health and status endpoints answer as published on every instance, and the app boots and serves its local features with either dependency unreachable.

Server boundary.
The server is same-origin only, enforces the published size limits and never serves source files or credentials.

Credentials stay on the server.
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

The green table composition.
The dark green table is the one constant surface, with one paper sheet centred on it in page view and separate paper cards on it in canvas view.

Paper, type and single accent.
Screens use hard-edged paper, a serif display face over a highly legible body face, and one accent used only for selection and focus.
/app/run.json has string install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the app root lists every shipped package with its version and licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Shipped packages and bundled assets use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1 licences.
The product uses no datastore or external service beyond the provided Postgres and MinIO and the browser's own device storage.
The provided service configuration and credentials are left as given.
/app holds no virtual environment and no absolute symlinks.
The source language is TypeScript, and fonts and icons ship with the app and load from its own origin.
